newsitem.title: GERMANY: Banks lead advance on German share market.
newsitem.headline: Banks lead advance on German share market.

text.p: Bank shares returned to vogue on the German stock market on Wednesday, supporting steady gains in afternoon trade.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was up 56.58 points, or 1.66 percent, at 3,430.70 points at 1443 GMT, amid gains of four and five percent on leading bank shares.
June DTB DAX futures were up 51.5 points at 3,445.5.

Dealers said fresh rumours were circulating about possible takeovers in the banking industry, fuelled by the tantalising glimpse of a hostile takeover bid furnished by last week's now abandoned bid by steel group Krupp AG for rival Thyssen.
Deutsche's results, which had been released on a preliminary basis already, were broadly in line with expectations.

Broader gains were supported by the dollar's recovery while Tuesday's decline on Wall Street after the U.S. interest rate hike had minimal influence. Dealers said the mood was generally relief that the rate hike had finally gone ahead.

All the same, the market pared some of its gains after Wall Street started out slightly weaker on Wednesday and dealers said any further weakness in the U.S. market could take the shine off German shares too.
The top takeover candidates among the big banks, Bavaria's Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel-Bank AG and Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, were among the biggest gainers.

Dresdner Bank AG declined comment on a rumour that it was buying up shares in Hypo Bank. But it denied talk that its equity research team had recently recommended not selling Hypo shares, saying it had had a hold recommendation on Hypo for months.
Deutsche Bank was also well ahead, up 1.38 marks at 93.30 marks after giving details of its 1996 earnings.

Shares in Daimler-Benz AG got an unexpected late boost after it reported preliminary 1996 earnings data and said it planned to propose a dividend of 1.10 marks per share, after omitting any dividend in 1995.
The stock hit an all-time high of 136 marks, up 4.4 percent, by 1525 GMT.
